To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alkali-earth monocations, in particular calcium monocation, can abstract a halogen atom from a chloro- or a bromomethane molecule to form a metal halogen cations and a methyl radical.
the reactions of Mg(+), Ca(+)/CH3X, Sr(+)/CH3Br, and Ba(+)/CH3Cl, X = Cl, Br, proceed through a barrierless process and are exothermic.
The reactions of alkaline-earth monocation with chloro- and bromomethanes are endothermic or exothermic and the activation barriers are either very low (Mg(+)) or nonexistent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the gas phase reactions between alkali-earth metal ions (Mg(+)-Ba(+)) and chloromethane/bromomethane, which have been theoretically studied at the Density Functional level of theory.
the study of the reactions in the gas phase between alkaline-earth monocation and CH3Cl/Br.
the reactivity of alkaline-earth cations toward the simplest halomethanes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alkaline-earth monocation can abstract the halogen atom from chloromethanes and bromomethanes to give the corresponding halogen cation.

the halogen atom in the chloro- or the bromomethane molecule can be abstracted by the alkaline earth monocations, in the gas-phase, in a barrierless process, and the reaction rates can be estimated by conventional/variational transition state theory.

the alkaline earth monocations can abstract a halogen atom from CH3Cl and CH3Br to form the metal halogen monocations, but the process is only possible when the metal cations have at least two valence electrons, i.e., for Ca(+) and heavier alkaline earth monocation species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reactions between the alkaline earth monocations and CH3X are barrierless, exothermic processes.

the alkaline-earth monocation reactivity with chloro- or with bromomethane is strongly dependent on the size of the metal atom, with the larger alkaline-earth monications being more effective for the activation of the C-Hal bond.

, in the gas-phase, the alkaline-earth monocation Mg(+) cannot activate the carbon-halogen bond in chloro- and bromomethanes, whereas calcium, strontonium and barium monocations are able to activate the same bond.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in spite of the high ionization potential of the alkaline-earth monocation, the carbon-halogen bond in CH3X (where X = F, Cl or Br) is weak enough to be cleaved.
the alkaline-earth monocation can be used as an alternative catalyst in the halogen-abstracting reactions.
the reactivity of these systems can be understood in terms of the ionization potentials of the reactants and products, and that the reactivity decreases in the series of alkaline-earth monocation.
